<reason>Both sides were strong, but B built the cleaner decision rule and landed the more damaging catches. B correctly identified that the motion's distinctive claim is the word "over," then exploited A's own line that "the destination of the cargo is a detail; its content is the argument" to show that A's best material (value capture, jobs, volatility, Korea, Indonesia) supports processing rather than regional-over-global orientation — a burden A only partly discharged. B also owned the undisputed binding constraint (power costs, thin ports, expensive credit), and A's reply that these bottlenecks are fixable effectively conceded that destination priority is not what unlocks factories. B's turn on Indonesia (Chinese capital, Chinese demand, cheap coal, single 280m-person market) converted A's best example against it, and Australia/Botswana/Chile answered A's "luckiest exception" line with a pattern rather than a one-off. A fought back well: the "CON opposes nothing / process more and sell globally is the motion's core" reframe was its best move, and A answered the pressure questions concretely with three named policies and a coherent story that a graduated levy shifts rather than destroys forex earnings. That answer was better than B's closing dismissal ("a levy that bites must cost money") admitted. But A's regional-demand case remained answered by B's scale-and-fragmentation point (fifty-four customs regimes, low incomes) plus the consumer cost of the required external tariff, and A never produced an example of industrialization by deprioritizing rich-market exports. B's clipped rebuttal is a real execution cost, but the substance survived. Narrow but real edge to B.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>B's use of A's own concession that "the destination of the cargo is a detail" [B2.1-B2.2] to argue that half the motion had been abandoned, reinforced by the Indonesia turn showing that value-addition success story was built on serving distant rich markets inside a single unified market, not on regional priority.</best_rebuttal>
